VQActFlow tokenizes robot actions with a VQ-VAE and trains a diffusion transformer with Variational Flow Matching to predict categorical distributions over the codebook. Because action modes are discrete, the policy can be steered at inference time with classifier-free guidance on language and a lightweight codebook critic.

**Highlights**

- LIBERO-Goal 73.0 → 81.0%; LIBERO-90 80.5% vs. 77.2% (CFM), 72.4% (MT-ACT).
- Unitree G1 humanoid, 4 pick-and-place tasks: 23.8 → 57.5% success, wrong-task rate 41.3 → 2.5%.
- ALOHA-style bimanual, 4 contact-rich tasks: 45.0 → 77.5%; the CFM baseline failed all four.

**My contributions**

- Led the LIBERO-Goal / LIBERO-90 experiments and the codebook ablation.
- Collected the Unitree G1 teleoperation dataset (TWIST2 VR, 140 demos/task) and led G1 deployment and evaluation on four pick-and-place tasks.
- Ran the ALOHA-style bimanual experiments (four contact-rich tasks, 75 demos/task).
- Engineered inference latency to 155–350 ms per action chunk on an RTX 5090.
- Contributed to the VQ-VAE tokenizer, VFM objective, guidance (CFG + codebook critic), and matched-protocol baseline reproduction (CFM, MT-ACT, VQ-BeT, Discrete Policy + CFG).
- Co-wrote the manuscript and the RA-L revision.
